previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic migraines, pseudotumor cerebri, and other comorbidities was admitted after an episode of syncope followed by persistent lightheadedness and gait instability. She had poor oral intake and took glyburide without eating, raising concern for hypoglycemia, though she lacked typical symptoms. Initial evaluation showed new EKG changes but negative cardiac enzymes. MRI/MRA revealed no acute stroke but mild stenosis of the right vertebral artery and small vessel ischemic disease. Given recent URI symptoms and clinical findings, labyrinthitis was diagnosed as the likely cause of her vertigo and ataxia. A urine toxicology screen was positive for cocaine, leading to discontinuation of propranolol due to cardiovascular risks. Her blood pressure and glucose were managed during admission, and she was discharged home with a walker, home physical therapy, and updated medications, including permanent discontinuation of propranolol and counseling to cease cocaine use.
